title: Key questions as Infantino faces Fifa executives
description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino will face senior leaders of football's world governing body on Wednesday. This is what is expected to happen.
fullText:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino will meet with senior leaders of football's world governing body on Wednesday as criticism of his now scrapped plan to sell off Fifa's commercial and event operations intensifies.

After secretary general Mattias Grafstrom sent a highly critical internal memo to Fifa staff, Infantino summoned members of the Fifa management board to Morocco.

Tuesday also saw chief of global football development Arsene Wenger insist he was "not involved" in Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, adding that aborting it was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Prince Ali, president of the Jordanian Football Association, then accused Fifa of creating a situation which "amounts to blackmail" over unpaid prize money and support for Infantino's re-election.

These claims have not been verified by the BBC, and Fifa made no comment when approached. But Prince Ali's statement is indicative of the strength of feeling among the member associations that oppose Infantino.

At the weekend, Uefa said it had lost confidence in Infantino's leadership. Several member associations - including Wales, with England set to follow suit - have withdrawn support for his re-election.

Now Infantino will meet with Fifa's hierarchy to try to secure his position.

BBC Sport understands the meeting will take place at Fifa's Africa office in Rabat.

It will include Grafstrom and members of the Fifa management board.

Among those in attendance will be finance chief Thomas Peyer, legal chief Emilio Garcia Silvero, chief of staff Daniel O'Toole, chief of member associations Elkhan Mammadov and media relations director Bryan Swanson.

It is unclear the intention of the meeting, but it is expected that Infantino will attempt to build bridges in an attempt to create a path to remaining as president.

However, this may not be straightforward.

In his letter to Fifa staff, Grafstrom said the events of the past week had been "a sad and reproachable series of events" which were "difficult to comprehend and accept".

On Friday, Kevin Lamour, Fifa's chief operating officer, said the private investment plan was "the project of one person". He added Fifa's own administration was "deceived".

Infantino will have to show contrition and perhaps offer a route to reform if he is to win back the support of his inner circle.

Carlos Cordeiro, Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance, quit on Friday over the plan.

Cordeiro said the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

Member associations had been given a deadline of 19 September to approve the plan or miss out on the extra funding that came as part of the deal.

In his resignation announcement, Cordeiro offered a series of questions which Infantino will likely face at Wednesday's meeting.

"Most troubling of all," Mr Cordeiro said, "is the absence of answers to fundamental questions.

"Why this deal? Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football?

"These questions remain largely unanswered, and yet member associations are being asked to make a decision of enormous consequence in barely 50 days or risk being left behind.

"That is not a responsible way to determine the future of the world's game.

"This proposal has become a defining question for Fifa's future."

On top of this, Infantino may also have to map out - or could offer - a route for reform.

This may involve putting additional checks and balances in place that would make it impossible for such a plan to be devised and presented in this way again.

Perhaps he could shelve his plans for a 64-team World Cup? Or offer to open up Fifa's cash reserves?

Courting controversy and befriending Trump - the story of Fifa boss Infantino

Infantino calls executive meeting as criticism mounts

Infantino opponents threaten 'non co-operation' with Fifa

It seems unlikely that Infantino will leave his position as Fifa president by the end of Wednesday.

Infantino has, so far, shown no indication he is considering relinquishing his position. Indeed, he has been trying to rally his core supporter base around the globe.

On Tuesday we saw African countries Egypt, Morocco, Niger, Mauritania and DR Congo all issue statements in support of Infantino.

Infantino will, however, have to answer serious questions about a hugely controversial and damaging week for Fifa.

There may be those in the room who will query his ability to turn this around, especially with such fierce criticism from European countries.

Could that criticism be strong enough for Infantino to tender his resignation?

More likely, perhaps, Infantino could see this as the start of the fightback.

We may see a statement that will include an apology and a promise of change.

If Infantino does vow to fight on, Uefa and countries from other confederations must look to find other ways to oust him.

The Fifa Council could try to force Infantino's hand through an emergency meeting.

Such a gathering would be triggered if 19 of the 37 Fifa Council members call for one.

However, BBC Sport understands there are doubts that the 19 votes could be achieved.

Another step could be an extraordinary congress of the 211 Fifa member associations, which would be held if one-fifth, or 43 associations, "make such a request in writing".

So Uefa, which has 55 nations, can trigger the extraordinary congress whenever it wishes.

That would take a minimum of two months from the point it is triggered, but more likely three months, and there is no guarantee of success.

In effect, it would be a de facto election without there being another candidate as 106 votes would be needed to pass the vote of no confidence.

Infantino would have time to win back votes from those who had been angered by the investment plan.

Uefa can only really go down this route if it is confident of getting over the line.

Which leaves finding a suitable candidate to fight the election at the Fifa Congress in March.

Infantino stood unopposed when he was re-elected in 2019 and 2023 and if someone wants to battle him for the position, the deadline to announce their candidacy is 18 November.

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is seen as the most likely unity candidate to stand against Infantino.

But there should be no expectation of success. Even at the height of the Fifa scandal in 2015, Sepp Blatter was re-elected as president eight days before he eventually resigned.

If Infantino is still in position later on Wednesday, this story could yet have a long way to run.

Inside Fifa, the expectation is that Infantino has called the meeting in Rabat in an attempt to clear the air, have a show of unity and try to achieve some alignment with his senior staff.

But while that may be the beleaguered president's intention, what remains uncertain is what kind of response he will receive from those present, especially given the highly critical statements issued in recent days by chief of global football development Wenger, secretary general Grafstrom and chief operating officer Lamour.

Some staff are asking if that could have emboldened others at the top of the organisation to speak out against him or to even insist he steps down.

It is no surprise Infantino has chosen Morocco, where he has been based over the past week.

Morocco is friendly territory for him. Not only is the country hosting the next World Cup, its national football association has come out in support of him. And it is where he still hopes to be re-elected for a fourth term at next year's Congress.

The Uefa-led rebellion against him will be hoping that it does not get that far, and that he has been forced to quit long before then.

title: Nazi warships, mammoth bones emerge as Danube River dries up
description: Water levels on the Danube River have dropped so low that dozens of World War II German battleships – and even the remains of an ancient woolly mammoth — are emerging into view.
fullText:
Water levels on the Danube River, the second longest in Europe, have dropped so low because of drought that the hulks of dozens of World War II German battleships — and even the remains of an ancient woolly mammoth — are emerging into view.

They are a curious distraction from the summer heat crisis. The Danube's record-low water levels have also forced power plants to the brink of shutting down, and governments across Central and Eastern Europe are taking steps to conserve electricity.

In the middle of the river separating Serbia and Romania, near the Serbian port of Prahovo, a rusty hull is now visible, along with a broken mast where the Nazi flag once flew.

The ships, some still laden with weapons, belonged to Nazi Germany's Black Sea fleet that the Germans deliberately sank as they retreated from Romania and as Soviet forces advanced deeper into Europe near the end of the war.

At least 20 World War II wrecks of various sizes are now visible to the naked eye from the banks of Prahovo.

Ivica Gavrilovic, who has spent his whole life living beside the Danube, said the interest in the wrecks was high but access remained difficult. "People still don't know how to access the ships themselves," he said, while taking a family of three out on his small boat.

Historians say up to 200 German warships were scuttled in September 1944 near Prahovo in the Danube gorge as they came under Soviet fire. The idea behind the deliberate sinking was to slow down the Soviet advance in the Balkans. But Nazi Germany surrendered months later, in May 1945.

The sight of the old warships is a reminder that the Serbian government, with European Union financial support, has long been trying to do something about them. Some were removed from the river by Communist Yugoslav authorities, but most have remained because of the explosives they carried.

Now, however, authorities are trying to keep traffic flowing on the Danube, which flows through 10 nations, as the dropping water levels create dangerous conditions. Experts have linked the unusually hot weather to global warming and other factors.

Krsta Brandic, a Prahovo resident, said the low water levels have almost stopped ship traffic: "As you can see, the (big) ships can't pass anymore."

The old vessels have emerged before. In 2024, a trove of sunken Nazi ships, still decked out with explosives, emerged in the Danube following a blistering summer drought. Dozens of scattered ships operated by Nazi Germany's Black Sea fleet also appeared in 2022 near Prahovo after water levels reached record lows.

Meanwhile, falling water levels in the Danube unveiled bones of a mammoth in Bulgaria, a local museum director told AFP.

The bone fragments found near the northeastern city of Ruse "very likely" belonged to a woolly mammoth that lived during the Ice Age, said Nikolay Nenov, director of the Regional Historical Museum.

Specialists have so far identified a jawbone, fragments of tusks, part of a shoulder blade, and a femur with its articular head among the stash, Nenov said.

The animal is thought to have been young and the dark color of the bones may indicate that it spent a lot of time in a marshy environment, he added.

The bones are an important discovery because they are well preserved and "unlike many previous discoveries ... were concentrated in the same place," indicating that they all belonged to the same animal, Nenov said.

Woolly mammoths coexisted with early humans who hunted the cold-resistant herbivores for food and used their tusks and bones as tools.

The animals died out about 4,000 years ago. For decades, scientists have been recovering bits and pieces of mammoth tusks, bones, teeth and hair.

title: Liverpool enter club to club talks to sign England international
description: Liverpool have entered club to club talks to sign an England international. Richard Hughes is rapidly running out of time to rescue what is becoming an increasingly uncomfortable transfer window.There...
fullText:
Liverpool have entered club to club talks to sign an England international.

Richard Hughes is rapidly running out of time to rescue what is becoming an increasingly uncomfortable transfer window.

There is still a chance to turn things around before the deadline, but as things stand, there is a growing feeling that Andoni Iraola is being asked to perform miracles with an unbalanced squad.

Nobody expected the new Liverpool head coach to inherit a perfect team. That much was obvious the moment he walked through the door. The expectation, however, was that Hughes would use the summer to reshape the squad around Iraola's demanding, high-intensity style of football.

Instead, Liverpool have spent much of the window pursuing Bradley Barcola and Yan Diomande. Diomande has now rejected a move to Anfield, while Paris Saint-Germain continue to hold firm over Barcola's valuation. Liverpool may yet land one of their priority targets, but the drawn-out pursuit has come at a cost.

While attention has been fixed on signing another winger, glaring weaknesses elsewhere in the squad remain.

With just over two weeks until the Premier League season begins, Liverpool's defensive depth already looks alarmingly thin.

Joe Gomez and Jeremy Jacquet are both sidelined with injuries, Giovanni Leoni is still working his way back from the ACL injury that ended his previous campaign, and Conor Bradley faces another spell on the sidelines after suffering yet another fitness setback.

The result is that Iraola has spent pre-season patching together makeshift defensive units rather than building the partnerships and understanding that every new manager desperately needs. Pre-season should be about implementing ideas and creating cohesion. Instead, Liverpool have simply been trying to get enough defenders onto the pitch.

Right now, Virgil van Dijk is the only senior centre-back fully available.

Youngsters have stepped up admirably. Ifeanyi Ndukwe has impressed throughout pre-season and shown he looks comfortable at the level. Unfortunately, he is unlikely to remain at Anfield this season because he does not currently satisfy the work permit requirements and is expected to head out on loan. Mor Talla Ndiaye and Luke Chambers have also been handed opportunities, but both are naturally more comfortable on the left side of the defence.

Things should improve once players return. Jacquet's injury is not thought to be serious, Gomez is edging closer to fitness and Leoni should soon be back in full training.

But should Liverpool really be relying on that?

Gomez's injury record makes him difficult to count on across a full campaign, while both Jacquet and Leoni are completely untested in the Premier League and are themselves returning from injuries. That is hardly the foundation of a title-chasing defence.

The concerns extend beyond the centre of defence too. Bradley's fitness problems are becoming an unfortunate pattern, having missed more than 20 matches through injury in each of his three seasons with the first team.

Jeremie Frimpong offers an attacking alternative, but asking him to play as a traditional right-back every week would take away many of the qualities that make him such an exciting player.

Liverpool still need another winger. That much is obvious. But the longer this window goes on, the clearer it becomes that the defensive rebuild deserves just as much attention.

If Hughes fails to address it before the season begins, Iraola could find himself fighting with one hand tied behind his back before a competitive ball has even been kicked.

It looks like the club's sporting director is working on it though. TuttoJuve claim that England international Fikayo Tomori has ended up on Liverpool's radar as they look to bring in an experienced centre-back.

The report goes as far to say that Liverpool have even initiated exploratory club to club talks with AC Milan in order to determine how feasible a move would be.

So, it looks like Tomori is one to keep an eye on.

fullText:
Arsene Wenger has come under fire for standing by and allowing FIFA to "sell" the World Cup, which has forced the Arsenal icon to distance himself from the proposal.

Wenger has been working at FIFA since leaving his role as Arsenal manager in 2018 and appears to play an important role within the organisation. This meant many believed proposals of that nature would have passed through him and that he should have stopped them before they reached the public domain.

However, that did not happen and FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under serious pressure to resign following the controversial proposal. Other FIFA officials who did not step down and were perceived to have allowed or supported the proposal have also faced significant criticism in recent days.

Wenger has been among those criticised, but he has now explained his role within the organisation to make it clear that he was never involved in the proposal when it was drafted.

He said, as reported by Give Me Sport:

"The recent events at FIFA deserve some clarity from my side.

"At FIFA, I am the Chief of Global Football Development.

"Together with my team, I oversee the data analysis of the game, the FIFA online training centre, the development of youth education through 60 academies across 60 countries where they are most needed, and youth competitions around the world.

"In addition, I am a technical adviser to IFAB.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger's statement was intended to clarify his responsibilities within FIFA and distance himself from the proposal. He stressed that his work focuses on football development rather than strategic planning, while reaffirming his belief in an independent FIFA that operates with commitment, transparency, and integrity.

fullText:
Since Stardew Valley rejuvenated the farming sim genre a decade ago, games like Fields of Mistria are capitalising on its popularity with their own special touches

Farming simulator games deliver on an escapist fantasy: going off-grid from the modern work grind, in exchange for charming small-town life and a farm to call your own. While these games have had dedicated fans since the days of Harvest Moon, the most popular today, Stardew Valley, contemporised the genre with a larger range of activities and lovable townspeople to befriend and romance. Created in 2016 by independent developer Eric Barone, it has now sold more than 50m copies and become the mould for so many other indie farming sims.

Fields of Mistria is one of these farming sims in a post-Stardew world – though it updates the core formula. Created by independent developer NPC Studio, Fields of Mistria has already proven popular: it debuted in early access (a pre-release version of the game meant for early players to find bugs and give feedback) for PC players on Steam in August 2024, and in the first month the game racked up more than 4m player hours. It’s for a good reason: Mistria satisfies all of those same farming sim desires but with more expansive character creation and a story steeped in magic.

Fields of Mistria is a farming and life simulator game with fantasy themes. You play as the new farmer in Mistria, a lovable small town in recovery from an earthquake, whose inhabitants hope you’ll fulfil their requests for various produce and supplies. Over the four seasons you grow crops, raise barn animals and attend events: from regular Saturday markets to the annual Shooting Star festival. Choose between a cat or a dog as a pet and accumulate toys and accessories for all your animals. My personal favourite is watching a duck and a rabbit play together on a seesaw.

You’ll repair structures and buildings in town, such as the bridge or the Sleeping Dragon Inn. Donate supplies and funds, raise your renown level and town rank, and restore Mistria to its former glory. Along the way you’ll make friends with the townspeople: like Ryis the carpenter, who is shockingly quick at those repairs, or Hayden, the owner of Sweetwater Farm who has a haughty prize-winning chicken called Henrietta (and yes, you can befriend her, too).

You can also fish, catch bugs and explore the mines; just be careful about selling anything immediately, because you might want to hold on to it to donate to the museum, or use it to craft cute furniture for your home. Your character evolves along with you: the more you do, the more you’ll be able to level up skills such as cooking, ironmongery, and archaeology.

Fields of Mistria may sound like a classic farming sim – but there’s a twist: you gain magical powers, thanks to the mysterious dragon Caldarus, who you can talk to by visiting a shrine on your farm. One spell lets you create rain, so you don’t have to painstakingly water all of your crops. Another lets you fully restore stamina, so you can get back to fishing for that golden eel. It seems the earthquake may have unearthed some unexpected parts of Mistria’s history.

And while Stardew Valley – despite its lauded queer relationship options – has thus far only offered two choices for gender expression, in Mistria, character gender options also include “they/them”, “she/they,” “he/they,” and more.

There are also some great accessibility features. In particular, you can make a day longer by slowing down time, giving yourself a truly leisurely pace to play. It’s an antidote to how frantic Stardew Valley can feel, especially during special events when you’re trying to pack as much into a day as you can.

Mistria is full of potential suitors, and you can woo any eligible villager regardless of gender. There’s Juniper, the sorceress who owns the local bathhouse, and who wouldn’t look out of place with the cast of Sailor Moon. Or maybe you’d like to romance March, the grumpy blacksmith who is a tough nut to crack – he’s a tsundere, an anime archetype for someone who’s abrasive at first – until you know him better.

Early access capped the number of hearts you could unlock with each villager, and players have been eagerly awaiting the extended romance arcs in the full game. Without spoiling too much, let’s just say there’s also at least once romance option who isn’t exactly human.

This lively cast of characters and love interests is ultimately what makes Fields of Mistria a standout in its genre. The town is always alive and bustling, encouraging you to spend time there – Friday nights at the Inn, where everyone gathers, being a highlight. Some of the villagers play Dungeons and Dragons, while others try out new desserts. You can ask socialite Elsie for gossip, or even join the kids in an adventuring club. There’s a real sense of place and kinship that makes playing Fields of Mistria feel like a lovely escape.

title: Palantir paid just £2m corporation tax in UK in 2024 despite lucrative public sector contracts
description:
Software group benefits from global systems and accounting practices ‘that enable tax to be shirked’, says union boss
The software group Palantir paid just £2m in corporation tax in the UK in 2024, despite holding public sector contracts worth hundreds of millions, thanks to tax breaks that are likely to reduce its contributions to governments around the world for years to come.
The US-headquartered company, which has harnessed AI to secure lucrative work for the NHS and the Ministry of Defence, is growing exponentially.

fullText:
Software group benefits from global systems and accounting practices ‘that enable tax to be shirked’, says union boss

The software group Palantir paid just £2m in corporation tax in the UK in 2024, despite holding public sector contracts worth hundreds of millions, thanks to tax breaks that are likely to reduce its contributions to governments around the world for years to come.

The US-headquartered company, which has harnessed AI to secure lucrative work for the NHS and the Ministry of Defence, is growing exponentially.

Palantir’s shares bounced 17% in early trading on Tuesday after its chief executive, Alex Karp, forecast worldwide revenues would almost double this year to $8bn (£5.95bn), a result that he described as “otherworldly”.

But the amount of tax Palantir pays compared to profits earned – its effective tax rate – is just 1.4% globally, according to a report published on Wednesday by the Centre for International Corporate Tax Accountability and Research (Cictar).

In the US last year, the company paid nothing in federal taxes and just over $2.5m in state taxes, the report states.

Andrea Egan, general secretary at the trade union Unison, which commissioned the report, said: “Systems that enable tax to be shirked on an industrial scale clearly have to change. The likes of Palantir need to stump up what’s due. Tech giants raking off billions in profit shouldn’t be free to pay what they please. Ministers shouldn’t award contracts to run public services to firms that are starving them of cash.”

The UK is Palantir’s biggest market outside the US, with £247m of revenues declared by the company for 2024, the most recent year covered by the report, while the majority of its non-US workforce – about 750 employees – are based in Britain.

As of 2026, Palantir holds an estimated £670m in government contracts. A three-year, £240m deal with the MoD was awarded last December without a competitive tender.

In 2024 the company paid just £2.1m in UK corporation tax, despite declaring profits of over £25m, giving an effective tax rate of just over 8%, researchers found. The UK corporation tax rate was 25% that year and remains at that level.

Despite the size of the UK market, tax collected here was less than in South Korea, Japan, France or Germany.

One reason, according to the researchers, is that Palantir is accounting for its UK revenues in the US, a practice sometimes referred to as transfer pricing. “A major pattern emerges of Palantir shifting revenues and profits from contracts in Europe to the US parent company to take advantage of the massive tax shelter it has created there,” they said.

While 26% of all Palantir revenue is sourced from customers outside the US, only 4% of revenue is booked abroad. The reason for this is not clear, but researchers said they believed contracts with customers were signed with Palantir’s US companies, which in turn paid a service fee to local country subsidiaries to deliver the work.

For example, Palantir disclosed £159m of revenues in its UK company filings for 2024, but disclosed £247m of UK revenues in its stock market filings.

A spokesperson for Palantir said the company complied with the tax regimes in the jurisdictions in which it operated, and criticising its use of transfer pricing was “simply not credible”. They said: “Transfer pricing, which allocates a company’s profits among entities within the Palantir group of companies, is an entirely standard practice that is virtually universal for large multinational companies.”

They said accounting practices could lead to different filings in different countries, and it was common for US parent companies, as the ultimate owners of the products sold, to record revenues earned abroad.

Another way in which Palantir cuts its tax bill is by granting share options to staff. The company can reduce what it owes by the amount the shares are worth when they vest. Employees are liable for income tax on their share options, often at higher rates, but the use of shares rather than cash to pay staff shifts the tax burden from the company to its employees.

A Palantir spokesperson said this was “a completely standard tax measure established under the previous Labour government [in the UK]”, designed to give employees a real stake in a business. “Crucially, it means that more tax is paid because corporation tax is 25%, whereas for these shares, income tax, which is higher, is due.”

In the US, Palantir has stored up billions in tax credits from share options, and losses carried forward from previous years, meaning that at the current rate of profit, it would not be liable for US federal income tax payments for “nearly a decade”, the report states.

Like other US companies, Palantir is also a beneficiary of tax cuts implemented under Donald Trump, who reduced the rate for corporations from 35% to 21% during his first term as president. In his second term, he negotiated a carve-out from an international agreement to impose a minimum tax rate of 15% on large multinationals.

“While profits are earned in European markets, much of that income is returned to the US in the form of related party payments,” the report states. “While some level of related party payments may be justified, it appears that Palantir’s efforts are intentionally and artificially reducing taxable income and income tax payments across its European operations.”

Palantir said it paid $148m in UK employment taxes last year, a figure that included employer national insurance contributions and some income tax paid on behalf of staff.

title: Next MLS Commissioner Berg Is Ready To Ride The FIFA World Cup Wave
description: Larry Berg, the next MLS commissioner, doesn't plan on sitting on his hands or the league's laurels, realizing the it needs to use the recent World Cup to grow even more.
fullText:
When he was eight years old while growing up in Cherry Hill, New Jersey, the father of Larry Berg saw a poster on a telephone pole about a new youth soccer league starting up.

"We basically had two teams," Larry said. "We played each other every weekend, and it grew from there. I fell in love with the game, and I learned about World Cups. I learned about the broader universe, and I became a student of the game. I became a fan of all the leagues that have been in the U.S. I certainly became a fan of the U.S. men's national team and ultimately a fan of Major League Soccer."

Today, he is more than a fan of MLS. He is the commissioner of the 30-team league.

Berg, 60, was introduced to the media at league headquarters in Midtown Manhattan on Tuesday as the successor to Don Garber, who will step down as commissioner after 27 years at the helm at the end of the year. He will become the third commissioner in league history. Doug Logan was the first, from 1996-99.

Berg, who will divest his interest as co-owner of the Los Angeles Football Club, will be concerned with more than just one team. He has been charged with leading MLS in riding the wave that the 2026 FIFA World Cup created.

"The foundation has been built," he said. "Now it's our responsibility to build on it, and that's what excites me most.

"I didn't accept this role to protect what we've already accomplished. I accepted it because I believe this league is ready for its next chapter. I believe Major League Soccer has entered a new era. The foundation is strong. The opportunity is extraordinary, and I have complete confidence that working together will seize it."

MLS must seize the opportunity for growth on the short and long term. The 1994 World Cup gave birth to the league. The 2026 World Cup can be a catalyst to boost it to an even higher orbit.

"The World Cup this summer reminded all of us why this sport captures the imagination of billions of people around the world. Millions of people across North America experienced that passion firsthand," Berg said. "They fell in love with the drama, the atmosphere, the supporter culture and the emotion that makes soccer unlike anything else.

"For many, it was also their first meaningful introduction to the global game, and that creates an extraordinary opportunity for all of us. The question isn't whether people are paying attention to soccer - they are. The question is what we do with this moment.

"Our responsibility now is to make sure the people discovering our league today become supporters for life. That means strengthening the connection between our clubs and their communities, creating unforgettable experiences for fans, and making sure the excitement generated this summer becomes lasting momentum for Major League Soccer."

While many teams boast capacity crowds, MLS needs to boost its streaming ratings.

When its 10-year, $2.3 billion deal with Apple TV was announced in 2023, fans needed an MLS Season Pass subscription to view matches. In 2025, the deal was cut to 2029.

When the deal winds up in 2029, the league will have to decide whether to renew with Apple or pursue other opportunities.

The deal ends in 2029, leaving MLS to decide whether to renew with Apple or pursue other partners.

Berg said that the next deal will be "finding media partners that want to co-create the future with us."

MLS is one of the few leagues in the world that doesn't include promotion or relegation. And during Berg's reign, he doesn't expect that to change.

"I can understand the appeal for the fan, [but] I don't think it's a great way to build a league," Berg said. "I don't think it's a way to get stadiums built and to get training facilities built and to have owners invest in rosters and all the other things you need to do. So I don't think it's appropriate for our league.

"I think Don has said before, never say never, but I just don't see it happening anytime soon."

During Garber's tenure, the league grew from 12 to 30 franchises. He helped concoct a plan to save the league from extinction when it dropped from 2 to 10 teams in 2001. Salaries rose appreciably. MLS attracted such top-notch players such as David Beckham and Lionel Messi. The former is still playing for Inter Miami CF.

Garber, who will become MLS chairman in 2027, had little doubt that the board of governors selected the right man to succeed him.

"In Larry, our league has found exactly the leader that we need at this time because, most importantly, Larry loves the game," he said. "He understands it because he helped build it. He knows our clubs and knows our league because he's experienced it full-time and understands the opportunities and the challenges ahead. He really understands that our best days are ahead.

"I will say that leading MLS is going to be one of the great privileges of your life, Larry. I think your integrity, your ambition, your thoughtfulness, your smarts, and your respect that you have for the game is going to help take this league to where we all want it to go."

title: Carlos Alcaraz Abandons Cincinnati Open Comeback, Sparks Ominous Reactions From Tennis World Ahead of US Open
description: Carlos Alcaraz’s comeback trail has suffered a major setback as the Spaniard has decided to withdraw from the Cincinnati Open, much to the dismay of the tennis community. Alcaraz, who has been sidelined since April due to a right wrist injury he sustained at the Barcelona Open, was set to make his highly anticipated return at the ATP Masters 1000 event in Cincinnati.
fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz's comeback trail has suffered a major setback as the Spaniard has decided to withdraw from the Cincinnati Open, much to the dismay of the tennis community.

Alcaraz, who has been sidelined since April due to a right wrist injury he sustained at the Barcelona Open, was set to make his highly anticipated return at the ATP Masters 1000 event in Cincinnati. However, he has opted to withdraw, sparking conjecture about his US Open title defense.

After missing the ATP Masters 1000 events in Madrid and Rome, being forced to skip his title defense at the French Open, and remaining absent from Wimbledon, Alcaraz sparked immense excitement when it was revealed that he would make his return at the Cincinnati Open.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion further raised anticipation by resuming full-intensity training ahead of the tournament, which is scheduled to begin on Aug. 13.

Despite appearing to make progress in his preparations, Alcaraz has pulled out of the Cincinnati Open. In a statement, tournament director Bob Moran confirmed the Spaniard's withdrawal and extended his best wishes to the world No. 2.

"We know Carlos is doing everything he can to get back to playing tournaments as soon as possible. We wish him the best with his recovery and look forward to welcoming him back to Cincinnati in the future," Moran said.

The news of the Spaniard's withdrawal rattled the tennis community, with Boris Becker among those lamenting the "sad" development.

"Bad news for Cincinnati and Carlos A …," Becker commented.

Tennis journalists Ben Rothenberg and Scott Barclay shared grim predictions about Alcaraz's US Open title defense and the remainder of his 2026 season, while reporter José Morgado expressed his surprise at the decision.

"I would assume Alcaraz will also be out of the US Open now, just because it would seem so daunting to come back from a major injury into a best-of-five tournament when totally cold. Although if he's ready, I am sure Winston-Salem could find a wild card for him…," Rothenberg said.

"I have to say, I don't think he plays again this year at this point. 😭," Barclay wrote.

"Now that's surprising," Morgado posted.

It remains to be seen whether Carlos Alcaraz will deem himself ready to compete at the US Open, with his title defense on the line. The New York Major is scheduled to begin on Aug. 30, leaving the Spaniard with a little over three weeks to regain full match fitness and mount his comeback.

title: Kilometer-high Saudi tower inches closer to world's tallest record
description: The JEC Tower has hit another milestone on its journey to become the new world's tallest skyscraper. The building is rapidly moving toward the halfway mark and has reached a height of 430 m (1,410 ft), with around 570 m (1,870 ft) left to go until the record-breaking megatall is completed.
fullText:
The JEC Tower has hit another milestone on its journey to become the new world's tallest skyscraper. The building is rapidly moving toward the halfway mark and has reached a height of 430 m (1,410 ft), with around 570 m (1,870 ft) left to go until the record-breaking megatall is completed.

Located in the port city of Jeddah, in Saudi Arabia, the JEC Tower (which also goes by Jeddah Economic Company Tower or Jeddah Tower) is designed by Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill, the former responsible for the design of the current world's tallest building, the 828-m (2,717-ft) Burj Khalifa. Once finished, this latest supertall will include at least 157 floors and will be almost twice the height of the tallest building in the USA, the 541-m (1,776-ft) One World Trade Center.

The tower has now risen to 107 floors, according to Saudi Prince Al Waleed bin Talal Al Saud, CEO of the Kingdom Holding Company which is developing the project. This makes it one of only a small number of buildings worldwide to surpass the 100-floor mark.

Currently, the plan is for its lower floors to host offices, with a 200-room luxury hotel above. Rising above these will be service apartments, a sky lobby, and multiple groups of residences, with the homes becoming more expensive – and expansive – as the building rises. Elsewhere will be multiple viewing points, plus a helicopter pad.

"As the first human-made structure to reach 1 kilometer (3,280 feet) in height, the design of Jeddah Tower is truly a pioneering engineering achievement," says Thornton Tomasetti, which is handling engineering duties. "First, we had to determine rational design wind loads at extreme elevations. Second, we had to control building movements, both lateral and vertical, over time. Third, our resulting structural system solutions had to be, above all, efficient and effective in their advancement of the ambitious architectural design. All easier said than done.

"Simplicity was key for constructability ease. Also, since the building was so large, we wanted to use materials judiciously. Our tall-building experts worked peer-to-peer alongside AS+GG and RWDI, pairing innovation and experience with advanced computational structural modeling and extensive wind tunnel testing. The outcome? An unparalleled structural system organization that supports the world's tallest building-to-be."

Though other major Saudi gigaprojects, like the Line and Mukaab, have faced major setbacks, the JEC Tower continues to rise with remarkable speed, with completion on this extraordinary skyscraper expected sometime in 2028.

description: Former world number one Iga Swiatek survived some nervy moments to launch her US Open build-up with a 6-0, 6-3 victory over Sara Bejlek in her second-round opener at the Toronto WTA 1000 on Tuesday.World number one Aryna Sabalenka was due to open her campaign on Tuesday night with a second-round clash against Japanese qualifier Moyuka Uchijima.
fullText:
Former world number one Iga Swiatek survived some nervy moments to launch her US Open build-up with a 6-0, 6-3 victory over Sara Bejlek in her second-round opener at the Toronto WTA 1000 on Tuesday.

In her first match since her Wimbledon title defense ended with a third-round exit, Poland's Swiatek was rolling through the first nine games, appearing in total control with a double-break for a 3-0 lead in the second.

But her Czech opponent dug in, using off-speed balls and some well-judged volleys to disrupt Swiatek's rhythm, winning two straight games before Swiatek pulled off a great escape -- fending off nine break points in a 22-minute sixth game to hold serve for a 4-2 lead.

"It was quite a weird game I've got to say," Swiatek gold Tennis Channel. "Not easy to finish it. There was much more running, much more different change of rhythm and different solutions that we used during that game.

"I felt like we both were kind of changing the rhythm and the pace all the time, so sometimes it was hard to adjust to it.

"I'm happy that I stayed in the game and stayed solid because I felt at the end it got pretty physical."

Swiatek has slipped from third in the world at this time last year to her current eighth.

Her Wimbledon disappointment came just four weeks after the four-time French Open champion bowed out in the last 16 at Roland Garros.

In fact, Swiatek has yet to reach a Tour-level final this season and is hoping a late surge over the North American hard court campaign capped by the US Open will prevent her from finishing the calendar year without a title for the first time since 2020 -- the year she won the first of her six Grand Slam titles at Roland Garros.

She took some of the extra time after Wimbledon to work on technical aspects of her game, saying she's been working on her rhythm and not rushing on the court.

"I feel like for sure in practices I already have these new habits in me. Sometimes during the match you've just got to focus even more to not let these old patterns come back."

World number one Aryna Sabalenka was due to open her campaign on Tuesday night with a second-round clash against Japanese qualifier Moyuka Uchijima.

Sabalenka is also looking to bounce back on the hard courts of North America after falling in the quarter-finals at Roland Garros and in the round of 16 at Wimbledon.

The Belarusian star has dominated on the surface this year, winning 23 of her 24 matches on hard courts -- the lone defeat her loss to Elena Rybakina in the Australian Open final.

In other early matches, ninth-seeded Ukrainian Elina Svitolina rallied from a set and a break down to beat Spain's Jessica Bouzas Maneiro 6-7 (5/7), 7-6 (7/4), 6-4.

Ukraine's French Open finalist Marta Kostyuk was also in action, taking on Canadian wild card Katherine Sebov.

title: Angels DFA former All-Star, World Series MVP Jorge Soler
description: Soler hit three home runs en route to winning World Series MVP with the Braves in 2021 and has been an All-Star since.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Angels have designated Jorge Soler for assignment, according to multiple reports, ending his time with the club.

The transaction removes Soler from their 40-man roster, and they now have seven days to either release him, trade him or place him on waivers. The move comes a day after MLB's trade deadline.

Soler, 34, is a former All-Star who won World Series MVP with the Atlanta Braves in 2021. Soler hit three home runs in the series that helped propel the Braves past the Houston Astros in six games. He played two seasons with the Miami Marlins after that World Series and was named an All-Star in 2023.

Soler spent the 2024 season split between the Braves and San Francisco Giants before joining the Angeles in 2024 via trade from the Braves. He's playing on the third year of a three-year, $42 million contract that he signed to join the Giants in 2024.

Soler has regressed at the plate this season with a slash line of .203/.291/.273 in 86 games. He's remained productive despite his diminished hitting with 12 home runs and 49 RBI. A former full-time outfielder, Soler has played primarily this season at designated hitter. The Angels are in last place in the AL West at 43-69.

Soler's 215 career home runs and postseason experience could make him attractive to a contending team seeking to add depth. Whether any team thinks it's worth taking on the remainder of his salary rather than wait for him to clear waivers or be released is another story.

title: Ireland's McFerran out of World Cup through injury
description: Distinguished Ireland goalkeeper Ayeisha McFerran is ruled out of the forthcoming Hockey World Cup through injury.
fullText:
Ireland's women must plan for the forthcoming World Cup without distinguished goalkeeper Ayeisha McFerran, who has been ruled out of the tournament through injury.

McFerran's many achievements in the game included being named Goalkeeper of the Tournament at the 2018 World Cup, at which Ireland were silver medallists.

Head coach Gareth Grundie has announced a 20-player squad to travel to Wavre, Belgium.

In McFerran's absence, Lizzy Murphy and Holly Micklem are named, offering them their first chance to potentially represent Ireland in goal on one of hockey's biggest stages.

The side will be making their third successive appearance at at a World Cup, having beaten Japan in a shootout in the bronze medal match in Santiago to ensure qualification for the 2026 edition.

Ireland, who are ranked 12th in the world, have been drawn in Pool C of the competition, and will face Spain in their opening match on 16 August, before playing New Zealand two days later and Belgium on 20 August.

A top-two finish in the pool would allow Ireland to progress to Pool E for a shot at a place in the semi-finals, while a third or fourth place finish would send them to Pool H where they will begin their final classification matches.

Meanwhile, Ireland men's coach Mark Tumilty has also announced a 20-strong squad as the side prepare to make their first appearance in the competition since 2018.

Tumilty has named an unchanged squad from that which secured qualification in Santiago in March courtesy of a comprehensive semi-final win over Wales, before coming from behind to beat France in the final.

Ireland's men are 10th in the world rankings and have been drawn in Pool C of the competition, taking on Australia in their opener on Sunday, 16 August, before facing South Africa and Spain on 18 and 20 August respectively.

As with the women, a top-two place would put the team into Pool E for a semi-final chance, while they would enter Pool H for classification fixtures if they come third or fourth.

Ireland women's squad: Elizabeth Murphy, Holly Micklem, Roisin Upton, Hannah McLoughlin, Caoimhe Perdue, Lena Neill, Sarah McAuley, Ellen Curran, Lisa Mulcahy, Sarah Hawkshaw, Charlotte Beggs, Michelle Carey, Christina Hamill, Mia Jennings, Katie Mullan, Sarah Torrans, Aisling Utri, Mikayla Power, Niamh Carey, Emily Kealy.

Ireland men's squad: Jaime Carr, Luke Roleston, Kyle Marshall (capt), Peter McKibbin, Mark McNellis, Sam Hyland, Gregory Williams, Fergus Gibson, Lee Cole, Luke Witherow, Sean Murray, Johnny McKee, Peter Brown, Adam McAllister, Matthew Nelson, Benjamin Walker, Jeremy Duncan, Ali Empey, Louis Rowe, Jonny Lynch.

title: Cape Verde coach Bubista resigns as Ivory Coast reappoint Renard
description: Head coach Bubista leaves Cape Verde after reaching the last 32 at the World Cup while Ivory Coast reappoint two-time Afcon winner Herve Renard.
fullText:
Bubista has resigned from his post as Cape Verde head coach to join Moroccan club RS Berkane while Ivory Coast have hired Herve Renard for a second spell in charge.

Bubista guided the island nation to the last 32 of the World Cup last month, where the Blue Sharks were beaten 3-2 by eventual runners-up Argentina after extra time.

The 56-year-old also reached the quarter-finals of the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations with Cape Verde, having taken charge in January 2020.

He has signed a two-year deal with RS Berkane, who finished second in the Moroccan top flight last season, and replaces Moin Chaabani, who has been appointed as Tunisia's new head coach.

Renard has won the Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) twice as a coach including with Ivory Coast in 2015. He previously led Zambia to a fairy tale title in 2012.

The Ivorians lost 2-1 to Norway in the last 32 at the World Cup and decided not to renew Emerse Fae's deal when it expired at the end of last month.

The former Nantes and Reading midfielder took over the reins midway through the 2023 Afcon - after the Elephants had failed in a bid to reappoint Renard - and the tournament hosts were crowned champions following a remarkable run through the knockout stage.

Renard has had stints with Morocco, Saudi Arabia (twice) and France's women since leaving Ivory Coast in May 2015, and was in the dugout for Tunisia for two games at this year's World Cup.

The length of the 57-year-old's contract has not been disclosed and the Frenchman is expected in Abidjan "in the coming days" to take up his official duties.

Bubista's sustained success with Cape Verde has raised his profile across the continent.

And while RS Berkane, from the north-east of Morocco, are not traditionally seen as one of the kingdom's big clubs they have enjoyed success in recent years.

They claimed their first domestic league title in 2024-25 and are three-time winners of the Caf Confederation Cup, Africa's second tier continental club competition.

Berkane caused controversy in 2024 by wearing a shirt in the Confederation Cup which featured a map of Morocco including the disputed territory of Western Sahara.

Cape Verde qualified for the World Cup for the first time ahead of Cameroon and the debutants proved to be the underdog story of this year's finals.

Cape Verde's football federation thanked Bubista for his "dedication, professionalism, and contribution to the development of the national team's sporting project" before wishing him "much success" in his future endeavours.

Bubista becomes the latest coach to leave one of the 10 African sides which appeared at the World Cup.

Vladimir Petkovic parted company with Algeria, who exited against Switzerland in the last 32, by mutual consent on Monday.

The 62-year-old Bosnian, who was appointed in February 2024, had extended his contract with the Desert Foxes until 2028 earlier this year.

Meanwhile, Hugo Broos stepped down as South Africa boss when his contract expired at the end of July, with the 74-year-old deciding to retire from management.

Senegal sacked Pape Thiaw in the wake of their dramatic last-32 exit against Belgium, with the country's football federation saying it had made the decision "in the best interests of Senegalese football".

The Teranga Lions have been linked with former France and Arsenal midfielder Patrick Vieira as a possible replacement.

Elsewhere, Tunisia appointed Chaabani on a four-year deal last month.

The 45-year-old replaced Renard, who himself took over the Carthage Eagles one game into their Group F campaign when Sabri Lamouchi was removed after a 5-1 defeat by Sweden.

Internal discussions are continuing at the Ghana Football Association after Carlos Queiroz led the Black Stars to the last 32, where the West Africans lost 1-0 to Colombia.

Queiroz appeared to announce his own departure on social media shortly after that defeat.

title: Nuclear Safety Authority supports spent nuclear fuel final disposal facility
description: On 4 August 2026, the Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority issued a statement to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment on Posiva Oy’s application for a licence to operate a spent nuclear fuel encapsulation and final disposal facility. According to STUK, the safety requirements required for granting the operating licence are met. This is the first time in the world that the geological final disposal facility for spent nuclear fuel has progressed to the operating licence phase.
fullText:
On 4 August 2026, the Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority issued a statement to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment on Posiva Oy’s application for a licence to operate a spent nuclear fuel encapsulation and final disposal facility. According to STUK, the safety requirements required for granting the operating licence are met. This is the first time in the world that the geological final disposal facility for spent nuclear fuel has progressed to the operating licence phase.

In its statement, the Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority (STUK) states that the encapsulation and final disposal facility for spent nuclear fuel Posiva built in Olkiluoto, Eurajoki meets the safety requirements set for it in the Nuclear Energy Act and Decree. Therefore, there is no obstacle to granting the facility an operating licence with regard to radiation and nuclear safety.

"This is a significant step in the final disposal of spent nuclear fuel that has been prepared for more than 40 years. STUK has been assessing and overseeing the safety of final disposal over several decades. Based on the overall assessment we have now made, we can conclude that the safety requirements for granting the operating permit are met," says Petteri Tiippana, STUK’s Director General.

The Government decides on whether to grant the operating licence for the final disposal facility based on preparatory work by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment. STUK’s favourable statement is a prerequisite for granting the operating licence. Even if the Government was to grant the operating licence, final disposal cannot yet be started. Before commencing operations, STUK shall confirm in a separate decision that the encapsulation and final disposal facility meets all safety requirements set for the start of operation.

In the final disposal solution selected by Posiva, the high-level spent nuclear fuel is enclosed in final disposal canisters in an above-ground encapsulation plant. The canisters will then be permanently placed in a final disposal facility built in the bedrock at a depth of 400–450 metres. The spent nuclear fuel is thus isolated from people and the living environment by several complementary release barriers. These include the final disposal canister made of iron and copper, the surrounding bentonite clay and the bedrock itself.

"The safety of final disposal is not dependent on a single structure or material. The safety is based on a combination of a canister, bentonite clay and bedrock, which prevents and slows down the release and migration of radioactive substances into the environment," says Jaakko Leino, Director of Nuclear Waste and Regulation.

Posiva is currently applying for an operating licence until the end of 2070. STUK will also monitor Posiva’s operations during the facility’s operation pursuant to the Nuclear Energy Act.

The safety assessment also covers long-term safety

In the safety assessment, STUK has examined both the safety of the encapsulation and final disposal facility during the operation phase and the long-term safety of the final disposal. The long-term safety assessment examines the development of the final disposal system and its environment over very long periods of time and how the release and transmission of radioactive substances into the environment is prevented and slowed down. In addition, STUK has assessed the readiness of Posiva’s organisation to start operation of the encapsulation and final disposal facility.

STUK’s statement is based on a long and thorough safety assessment. "Demonstrating safety has been the starting point for the assessment throughout. We have reviewed a great amount of technical data and safety analyses and monitored Posiva’s operations in many ways," says Antti Tynkkynen, Project Manager for the Posiva regulatory control project. Since 2000, STUK and its external experts have contributed a total of more than 250 man-years to project supervision and safety licence assessment.

Safety assessment and development continues

STUK proposes conditions for the operating licence to ensure the continuation of safety assessment and development also during the facility's operation.

STUK proposes that Posiva must carry out the first periodic safety assessment within ten years of granting the operating licence. At the same time, Posiva must update the long-term safety justification to correspond to the final disposal system to be deployed. In addition, Posiva must provide STUK with detailed plans for the final disposal facility for low- and intermediate-level waste and a safety justification for long-term safety based on them before the construction of the final disposal facility in question begins.

"As the operation phase begins, we will gain the first experience of how the plans, methodological tests and systems of the world’s first geological final disposal facility for spent nuclear fuel work in practice. These experiences must be used to learn and further develop the operations and safety, as necessary," Tynkkynen says.

Read more about this topic on the Posiva Final Disposal Facility page.

The Danube River's water is dropping so low that World War II ships are emerging
description: Water levels on the Danube River, the second longest in Europe, have dropped so low because of drought that the hulks of dozens of World War II German battleships are emerging into view.  The Danube’s...
fullText:
PRAHOVO, Serbia (AP) — Water levels on the Danube River, the second longest in Europe, have dropped so low because of drought that the hulks of dozens of World War II German battleships are emerging into view.

They are a curious distraction from the summer heat crisis. The Danube's record low water levels also have forced power plants to the brink of shutting down, and governments across Central and Eastern Europe are taking steps to conserve electricity.

In the middle of the river separating Serbia and Romania near the Serbian port of Prahovo, a rusty hull is now visible along with a broken mast where the Nazi flag used to fly.

The ships, some still laden with weapons, belonged to Nazi Germany's Black Sea fleet that the Germans deliberately sank as they retreated from Romania and as Soviet forces advanced deeper into Europe near the end of the war.

Historians say up to 200 German warships were scuttled in September 1944 near Prahovo in the Danube gorge as they came under Soviet fire. The idea behind the deliberate sinking was to slow down the Soviet advance in the Balkans. But Nazi Germany surrendered months later, in May 1945.

The sight of the old warships is a reminder that the Serbian government, with European Union financial support, has long been trying to do something about them. Some were removed from the river by Communist Yugoslav authorities, but most have remained because of the explosives they carried.

Now, however, authorities are trying to keep traffic flowing on the Danube, which flows through 10 nations, as the dropping water levels create dangerous conditions. Experts have linked the unusually hot weather to global warming and other factors.

Krsta Brandic, a Prahovo resident, said the low water levels have almost stopped ship traffic: "As you can see, the (big) ships can't pass anymore."

title: Big Walk review – larking around with mates elevated to an artform
description:

Radiant sunsets glinting on lapping waves; bushland valleys that beckon with secrets; modernist buildings sat atop craggy ridges: Big Walk’s setting is as arresting as it is beguiling – a kind of architectural fever dream transplanted to a handsome Australian wilderness – but it is the images created by players that lodge deepest in the mind. fullText:
Switch 2, PlayStation 5, PC; House House
The creators of Untitled Goose Game return with an online, open-world adventure that delivers slapstick silliness and bucolic majesty in nearly equal measure

Radiant sunsets glinting on lapping waves; bushland valleys that beckon with secrets; modernist buildings sat atop craggy ridges: Big Walk’s setting is as arresting as it is beguiling – a kind of architectural fever dream transplanted to a handsome Australian wilderness – but it is the images created by players that lodge deepest in the mind. Here’s one that has stuck with me: in the black of night, cicadas kicking up an almighty din, I had lost my partner. Panic. Despair. Fear. Then, there in the far distance, I saw him signalling in my direction. He was relentlessly spamming a gigantic, ball-shaped lamp on and off, the ground around him flicking from inky dark to warm pastel pink and back again, like a single Christmas light blinking from afar.

This kind of encounter is common in Big Walk, the brilliant and whimsical new online co-op puzzler from House House, the Melbourne-based studio behind the 2019 viral hit, Untitled Goose Game. Rather than playing as a honking, mischief-making goose as you do in that game, you are a bug-eyed, gangly limbed kind of bird person (think Pingu as drawn by Mondrian) for whom getting separated from your mates is all part of the fun. That’s somewhat because this rugged terrain is dense with vegetation and cliffs to fall down, and also because the game makes ingenious use of proximity and direction-based voice audio. Step out of earshot of your party and you will find it difficult to call for one another (unless, of course, you’ve picked up a Fisher-Price-like walkie-talkie).

So you and up to 12 players step out into this somewhat eerily photorealistic open world to uncover its mysteries. Quickly, you come across challenges which veer from the straightforward to the brain-scrambling: shoot the aforementioned ball-shaped lamp into a hoop; arrange wooden pegs decorated with odd, nature-themed symbols into some kind of shape. For each successfully completed task, you win what looks like a large red peanut. Get enough of these red peanuts and you score a key which in turn unlocks some important piece of infrastructure: for example, a slow-moving, toy-like train whose parping horns are a joy to obnoxiously blare across the otherwise bucolic landscape.

This structure naturally sustains its own rhythm: moments of intense cooperative concentration followed by longer stretches of ambulatory downtime. Such is the layout of this world, you end up doing a lot of backtracking. This is when a little of the game’s quirky lustre wears off since the actual walking is the least interesting part of Big Walk (and you’re also liable to get stuck on bits of rock). Frustration builds as you traipse through the same patch of scrub for the umpteenth time.

Still, Big Walk’s less action-packed moments can be gratifying in their own way: I never tired of watching the twinkling night sky segue with impossible speed into the warm, orange glow of a new day, or stopping to enjoy the sounds of a softly gurgling creak.

The beauty of Big Walk lies in how it tasks you with working together, conversing verbally and physically, to access its most enchanting sights. It stands out in an era when so much of online communication, be that in video games or on social media, has been distorted by a kind of attention-holding logic – for instance, the serotonin-releasing kerching of notifications or the relentless rewards of levelling up. Yet Big Walk eschews these pernicious aspects of digital life for a gentler, less overbearing experience that seems expressly designed to foster enriching connections and childlike playfulness.

Here’s another moment that has stuck with me: wiping away tears of laughter after my brother and I clumsily dropped one of those essential red peanuts to the bottom of the devilishly constructed, practically “masocore” 100ft shaft that we had painstakingly platformed our way out of. We nattered about it until we found the next thing that piqued our interest: wobbly rave tunes blaring from deep inside the belly of a mountain. I shan’t say any more: you and your pals will want to discover these delights for yourselves.

title: Fifa private money plan had to be scrapped - Wenger
description: Fifa's chief of global football development Arsene Wenger says the decision to scrap the plan to have private investment in Fifa competitions was "absolutely necessary".
fullText:
Fifa's chief of global football development Arsene Wenger says scrapping the plan to have private investment in Fifa competitions was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Fifa president Gianni Infantino planned to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, with external investors able to buy stakes.

Infantino had offered Fifa's 211 member associations $40m (£30m) each if they backed the proposal.

But after days of criticism - including Uefa's 55 nations threatening to boycott all Fifa tournaments - Infantino was forced to withdraw the plan.

Wenger has been in a role which encompasses data analysis of the game, Fifa's online training and youth competitions since 2019.

The former Arsenal boss previously supported Infantino's proposal to play the men's World Cup every two years.

A week after Infantino's investment plan was first released, the Frenchman issued a statement through Fifa in which he demanded "transparency and integrity" from world football's governing body.

"The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side," Wenger's statement read.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger is one of 18 Fifa officials named in a document preservation letter Uefa sent to Fifa threatening legal action.

Carlos Cordeiro - Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance - is the only Fifa official to resign over the scandal, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafstrom joined the criticism of the plan, writing in an internal memo to staff that the last week had been "difficult to comprehend and accept".

Grafstrom is seen as a close ally of Infantino, becoming Fifa's chief of staff after the Swiss was elected president in 2016. The Swede was evelated to secretary general, one of the most powerful positions in Fifa, in 2024.

"A sad and reproachable series of events - which were thankfully concluded with the project permanently abandoned - for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality," Grafstrom wrote.

"We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept.

"I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 member associations, hand in hand with all relevant stakeholders and in full compliance with the Fifa statutes and Fifa regulations.

"I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience. You do not need to worry.

"Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure."

Fifa has been approached for comment.

title: Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi meets Red Cross official
description: Aug 3 () - Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi met with a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross on Monday, after years of questions over the health and well-bein...
fullText:
Aug 3 (Reuters) - Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi met with a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross on Monday, after years of questions over the health and well-being of the 81-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner.

Suu Kyi has been in detention since February 2021, when an elected civilian government led ‌by her was ousted by Myanmar's military in a dawn coup, plunging the impoverished Southeast Asian nation into turmoil.

Since then, Suu Kyi's exact whereabouts and health condition have been ‌difficult to determine, with no foreign leader or envoy having publicly met with her despite requests for contact from countries in the region that have excluded Myanmar's leadership from their summits.

Suu Kyi met with Arnaud de Baecque, Resident Representative of ​the International Committee of the Red Cross to Myanmar, in the capital Naypyitaw on Monday, government spokesperson Khine Khine Soe said in a message via Telegram.

The ICRC confirmed that a delegate had met with Suu Kyi, without naming the official, while her son described the visit as the first positive development concerning his mother in more than five years.

In one of four photographs provided by the Myanmar government spokesperson, Suu Kyi is seen dressed in traditional Burmese attire and standing unaided, shaking hands with de Baecque.

In another, they are seated in a sparsely furnished, wood-panelled room containing only two chairs and a desk.

SON URGES CONTINUED ‌PRESSURE FOR SUU KYI'S RELEASE

The ICRC said the visit had met ⁠with its standards and procedures for visiting people deprived of liberty. "This included the opportunity to speak with Daw Aung San Suu Kyi in private," it said in a statement, using a Burmese honorific.

Suu Kyi's son, Kim Aris, told Reuters that the ICRC was not able to have a physician examine his mother ⁠but he said she seemed to be in good health and in good spirits.

"It's the first independent proof that I've had that she's actually alive for a long time now," he said in London. "So it's extremely meaningful."

Aris said that while he remained cautious, he hoped to be able to speak to his mother in time, and urged other governments to keep up the pressure on Myanmar to release her and other political prisoners.

Aris ​told ​Reuters in December that he had received only sporadic, second-hand details about his mother's heart, bone and gum problems - and ​had not heard from her in years.

The United Nations, whose special envoy on ‌Myanmar, Julie Bishop, has called repeatedly for independent, verifiable reports on Suu Kyi's circumstances, said it had taken note of the ICRC announcement and stressed the need for inclusive dialogue.

"We welcome this development and reiterate our call for the swift and unconditional release of all those arbitrarily detained, as a fundamental step towards conditions conducive to a credible and transparent political process," U.N. spokesperson Farhan Haq told a daily briefing in New York.

After a marathon run of secret trials following the 2021 coup, Suu Kyi, who was held under house arrest for a total of 15 years under a previous junta, was sentenced to 33 years' detention, convicted of charges ranging from corruption and inciting election fraud to violating state secrecy rules.

Her allies maintain that the charges were politically motivated and ‌aimed at sidelining the most popular politician in the country of 51 million people.

The sentence was later reduced, leaving ​her with 18 years still to serve, according to a member of her legal team.

Myanmar's military-backed administrations have repeatedly ​claimed that Suu Kyi, who is the daughter of Myanmar's independence hero General Aung San, ​is in "good health," even as international pressure has grown to allow independent verification.

After a meeting between Myanmar's foreign minister and counterparts from the regional ASEAN bloc ‌last month, Thailand's top diplomat Sihasak Phuangketkeow called for access to Suu Kyi.

ASEAN ​has barred Myanmar's leadership from its top meetings ​for failure to implement a peace roadmap.

In late April, following a military-engineered election that allowed former junta leader Min Aung Hlaing to become Myanmar's president, Suu Kyi was moved to house arrest.

In another of the photos provided by the Myanmar government offering a rare glimpse inside what appears to be her residence, Suu Kyi is seen cutting a birthday ​cake, with a clothes rack and storage boxes visible in the background.

A ‌fourth photograph is a close-up of the cake, inscribed with "Happy Birthday Aunty Suu 19.6.2026".

title: Van Gaal says he's open for a fourth coaching spell at Netherlands
description: Louis van Gaal said that he's open for a fourth coaching spell at the Netherlands national team. "I always want to help the Dutch Football Federation (KNVB), just as I also wanted to do at Ajax," Van Gaal told the Voetbal International in an interview published on Monday evening.
fullText:
Louis van Gaal said that he's open for a fourth coaching spell at the Netherlands national team.

"I always want to help the Dutch Football Federation (KNVB), just as I also wanted to do at Ajax," Van Gaal told the Voetbal International in an interview published on Monday evening.

"And with such a squad, there are of course possibilities. I also think that the Netherlands could still possibly become European or world champions, because 95% of the squad play abroad and often at good clubs."

Dutch media has suggested the 74-year-old as a potential successor to Ronald Koeman, who resigned following the Netherlands' early exit from the World Cup in North America last month.

Van Gaal said he's astonished with the fact that no ideal successor has been found so far and that coaches such as Arne Slot and Erik ten Hag have turned down the job.

"The only thing going on is that at this moment they still cannot get anyone and then my name comes up again. I find that rather unbelievable," he said.

"Four years ago at the World Cup in Qatar we lost on penalties in the quarter-finals and 'people' did not think our football was good enough. And those people now see me as the ideal man?"

He added that so far he hasn't had talks with the federation.

"I therefore have absolutely no idea what the KNVB wants," he said.

Van Gaal coached the national team in 2000-2001, 2012-2014 and 2021-2022. His best result was finishing in third at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil.

The KNVB will hope to find a new coach soon as their next game is on September 24 against Germany.

title: A youngster to watch - Veljko Milosavljevic

title: Itauma v Hrgovic upgraded to IBF world-title bout
description: British heavyweight Moses Itauma's fight against Filip Hrgovic on 29 August will be for the vacant IBF title.
fullText:
British heavyweight Moses Itauma's fight against Filip Hrgovic on 29 August will be for the vacant IBF title.

Itauma, 21, has been widely tipped as the next star of heavyweight boxing, with 12 knockouts in 14 professional victories.

Promoter Frank Warren told BBC Sport the IBF belt, vacated by Oleksandr Usyk in June, will be on the line at London's O2 Arena.

"A lot of people have high expectations of him as I have, by the way," Queensberry Promotions' Warren told BBC Sport.

"We signed him when he was 16. He was an amateur. We sponsored him and he turned professional with us. And he's been amazing and sort of taken the world by storm.

"This is a big moment for him. But I'm confident he can do it."

Itauma would become the youngest heavyweight champion since Mike Tyson if he beats Hrgovic.

He had initially been ordered to enter negotiations with Cuban Frank Sanchez for the vacant title and was given a deadline of 29 July.

However, Sanchez has agreed to step aside and will instead face the winner of the bout.

"We paid [Sanchez] some money. We said whoever wins the fight, you're not losing out and you'll get the opportunity to fight for the title against the winner," Warren added.

Itauma impressed in a fifth-round stoppage of American Jermaine Franklin in Manchester in March and stopped Briton Dillian Whyte in one round in August 2025.

Hrgovic, a 2016 Olympic bronze medallist, has won 20 professional fights. The 34-year-old stopped Briton Dave Allen in the third round in May.

"We know Hrgovic is going to come and give 100%, and 100% of him is hard work for anyone," Warren said.

Nigerian heritage key to my success - Itauma

Itauma handed everything on a plate - Hrgovic

A victory for Itauma could set up an all-British unification fight next year.

WBO champion Daniel Dubois defeated Fabio Wardley in May to become a two-time heavyweight world champion, and Warren confirmed the pair will contest a rematch in October.

Warren says should Itauma beat Hrgovic and then Sanchez, a fight against Ipswich's Wardley or Londoner Dubois for two world titles may take place at Wembley Stadium in 2027.

"It would be huge, absolutely huge. They're big punchers. These guys are big, big punchers. They're exciting. They're not in boring fights," Warren said.

Wardley and Itauma are both trained by Ben Davison, and Warren says the trainer will have to "make a decision" if the fight happens.

"I've seen best friends fight each other but they do it for the money they get, which pays the bills," Warren added.

Russian Murat Gassiev is the WBA champion, while Germany's Agit Kabayel holds the WBC title and is also signed to Queensberry.

Itauma could become the second-youngest British boxer in the modern era to win a professional world title. The Chatham fighter will be 21 years and 244 days old when the fight takes place.

Prince Naseem Hamed, at 21 years and 218 days, captured a world title at a younger age when he stopped Steve Robinson to win the WBO featherweight title in 1995.

Teddy Baldock won the vacant world bantamweight title against Archie Bell in 1927, aged 19 years and 346 days.

"Obviously I'm proud of what he's done up to now but if he does this I'll be the happiest guy around because he's such a nice guy," Warren said.

"He is a great advert for British boxing, world boxing and for sport."
